Superconductivity— the complete loss of electrical resistance at very low temperatures— was first observed by Dutch physicist **Heike Kamerlingh Onnes** on **8 April 1911** while experimenting with mercury in liquid helium. 

At that time the president of the United States was **William Howard Taft** (term: March 8 1909 – March 8 1913). Therefore, President Taft was in office when superconductivity was discovered.
